hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence and collapse to chance accuracy (e.g. runs 5, 6).
Lowering a very high learning rate rescues training from divergence, giving large gains (runs 11, 13, 14, 18).
At very small learning rates, 243 epochs underfit, so a step up helps (runs 1, 7).
Heavy L2 penalty underfits, so weakening it gives big gains (runs 91, 97, 100).
Increasing an already strong penalty worsens underfitting (runs 85, 86, 90).
Deeper networks are less stable at high learning rates, so removing a layer helps (runs 72, 75).
Wide deep networks with Adam are prone to instability, so reducing depth helps (run 72).
Deep networks diverge at high learning rates, so lowering the rate helps more at depth 3 (runs 11, 14, 18).
Deeper networks tolerate a learning rate increase worse, as shown by the large drops in run 5.
With a high learning rate, weaker regularization gives gains (runs 97, 100), unlike at low rates where the effect is negligible.
